description:
Astro-Tech is a multidisciplinary team passionate about space exploration, science, and technology. We bring together creativity, problem-solving, and technical skills to transform NASA's open data and resources into innovative solutions to real-world challenges.

Our mission is to explore beyond conventional thinking, experiment with emerging technologies, and build meaningful projects that combine science, engineering, and innovation.

Think beyond Earth. Build beyond limits.
summary: LAVA is an agentic RAG research platform for microgravity combustion and spacecraft fire safety. Fires in orbit have no buoyant plume, so flame spread and extinction are hard to predict, and the evidence is scattered across hundreds of NASA reports. LAVA indexes 376 NASA NTRS documents (~2.65M words, 10,062 chunks) plus NASA PSI experiment tables, and extracts 461 measurable findings across 8 campaigns (BASS-II, SAFFIRE, SAME, FLEX-2, ACME, CFI, SoFIE). An SI agent plans, retrieves with hybrid keyword + vector search, grades the evidence and answers with a citation behind every claim. Around the agent sits a research console: experiment explorer, comparison lab, smart-ranking explainer, coverage-and-gaps analysis, SI fire-safety insights and exportable research briefs. LAVA is not affiliated with or endorsed by NASA.
details: WHAT IT IS: LAVA is not just a chatbot. It is an agentic RAG platform: an SI research agent grounded in a structured NASA evidence base, plus a console of analysis tools around it. THE AGENT: For each question the agent plans sub-questions, retrieves evidence, grades whether it is enough, expands thin queries, synthesizes an answer and verifies each claim against the passage it cites. It keeps short-term (per conversation) and long-term memory with vector recall, and falls back to extractive answers if a model fails. RAG PIPELINE: A Python pipeline harvests NASA NTRS reports and PSI spreadsheets, cleans and deduplicates them, links them to experiments, extracts measurable findings (flame spread rate, limiting oxygen index, extinction time, pressure), chunks the text and embeds it into pgvector. Retrieval fuses keyword and vector search, then re-ranks with a weighted scorer, relevance gate, MMR diversification, PSI-row merging and an SI re-rank. DATA INDEXED: 376 NASA documents, ~2.65M words, 10,062 chunks, 461 extracted findings, 8 experiment campaigns and 10 facilities, plus NASA PSI tables stored as searchable rows. CONSOLE TOOLS: - Experiments Explorer: campaigns and facilities with linked documents, findings and PSI tables. - Comparison Lab: two campaigns compared condition by condition. - Smart Ranking: shows the score behind every retrieved passage. - SI Insights: curated fire-safety insight cards written by an SI core from the corpus. - Coverage & Gaps: empirical envelope and evidence-gap verdicts per campaign. - Measurements & Data: datasets with unit normalization and histograms. - Source Documents and Global Search over the whole corpus. - Research Briefs: multi-question reports exported to PDF/DOCX. - Mission Overview dashboard with charts. BENEFITS AND IMPACT: One checkable workspace instead of hundreds of scattered PDFs. Users see the exact evidence behind every sentence and can audit the ranking, which lowers the barrier to the literature for non-experts and supports faster reasoning about crew fire safety. TOOLS: React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Cloudflare Pages and Workers, Cloudflare Workers AI (embeddings), Neon Postgres with pgvector, Python (fastembed, pypdf). SI MODELS (via a multi-provider gateway with automatic fallback): - Flagship models through AgentRouter (agentrouter.org): GPT 6 Astra, GPT 6.1 Sol, GPT 5.6 Sol. - Free fast models: Google Gemini (free tier), Groq, Cloudflare Workers AI, and OpenRouter. CREATIVITY: Verified citations, an open ranking explainer that shows why each passage was chosen, PSI tables searchable as measured rows rather than prose, and PDF/DOCX export written from scratch. Every layer degrades gracefully if a component fails. FACTORS CONSIDERED: Trust over fluency, source fidelity to NASA's own text, auditability of every answer, and cost limits (free tiers, key-free local embeddings). TEAM ASTRO-TECH: Yousef (lead, backend, retrieval), Aynoor (frontend, UI), Yousef M. (data collection), Shahd (data cleaning). SI DISCLOSURE: In the product, SI models write answers and insight cards from retrieved NASA passages. Models used: GPT 6 Astra, GPT 6.1 Sol and GPT 5.6 Sol (via AgentRouter), plus free models from Google Gemini, Groq, Cloudflare Workers AI and OpenRouter. Automated tests were written with SI coding-agent assistance and reviewed by the team. The logo was cleaned up from a hand sketch with an SI image tool. The demo voice-over (if used) is synthetic audio. UI translations into several languages are machine-translated.
